detail: Individuals who were in foster care on their 18th birthday and are younger than 26.
notes: DHCS outreach letter phrases it as in foster care on 18th birthday and younger than 26.

detail: Exempt from the work requirement.

item: Parents and caregivers of young children
value: Exempt if caring for a dependent child age 13 or younger, or a disabled individual
detail: Parents, guardians, caretaker relatives, or family caregivers of a dependent child 13 years of age and under, or of a disabled individual, are exempt.
notes: DHCS member page: parents and caregivers of children ages 0-13. See flagged items for a wording inconsistency on the DHCS tracking page.

detail: Veterans with a full (total) disability rating are exempt.

Medically frail individuals or those with special medical needs that significantly impair their ability to comply; DHCS member materials include serious or complex ongoing medical conditions, serious mental health conditions, and disabilities.
Individuals meeting the TANF work requirements (CalWORKs in California) are exempt.
Members of a household receiving SNAP benefits who are not exempt from the SNAP work requirements are exempt.
Participants in a drug or alcohol rehabilitation or treatment program are exempt (DHCS includes those asked to attend treatment).
Inmates of a public institution are exempt.
Pregnant individuals or those eligible for postpartum coverage in their state; California covers pregnancy and 12 months postpartum.
A month counts if the individual was under age 19, or was eligible for or enrolled in Medicare Part A, or enrolled in Medicare Part B.
A month counts if the individual was released from jail or prison within the last 90 days.
A month counts if the individual got care in a hospital, nursing facility, or psychiatric facility.
A month counts if the individual traveled outside their area to get treatment for a serious medical condition.
A month counts if the individual lived in a county with very high unemployment or in a county affected by a federal natural disaster.

States may offer short-term hardship exceptions, for example: receiving inpatient or certain other medical services; needing to travel outside the community for certain medical care; residing in a county with unemployment at or above 8 percent or 1.5 times the national average; residing in a county where certain national emergencies or disasters exist.

item: Caregiver of a person with a chronic condition, disability, or functional limitation (state law)
value: Specified excluded individual - not subject to the requirement
detail: WIC 14005.69(b)(2)(F), as amended by AB 2161, lists as a specified excluded individual 'the parent, guardian, caretaker relative, or family caregiver of an individual with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation.'
notes: Broader than the federal caregiver-of-a-disabled-individual exemption.

item: Individuals in other mandatory Medicaid eligibility categories
detail: WIC 14005.69(f)(3), as amended by AB 2161, deems compliant 'an individual described in any of subclauses (I) through (VII) of Section 1396a(a)(10)(A)(i) of Title 42 of the United States Code.'

item: Any other federally required or approved exemption
detail: WIC 14005.69(f)(5), as amended by AB 2161: 'an individual excluded based on any other federally required or approved exemptions outlined in the state plan or waivers.'

item: Short-term hardship - inpatient or similar-acuity care
detail: WIC 14005.69(h)(1): inpatient hospital services, nursing facility services, intermediate care facility services for individuals with intellectual disabilities, inpatient psychiatric hospital services, or other services of similar acuity, including related outpatient care, and the individual requests the exemption.

item: Short-term hardship - Presidentially declared emergency or disaster
value: Automatic in California if the county qualifies
detail: WIC 14005.69(h)(2): the individual resides in a county in which an emergency or disaster was declared by the President under the National Emergencies Act or the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act. DHCS's Implementation Plan says DHCS will automatically provide this exemption.

value: Unemployment at or above the lesser of 8 percent or 1.5 times the national rate
detail: WIC 14005.69(h)(3), subject to a request from the department to the HHS Secretary. ACWDL 25-30 states the same threshold. DHCS's Implementation Plan notes the qualifying counties are 'not yet defined by CMS' and that DHCS will automatically provide the exemption.

item: Short-term hardship - travel for medical care
detail: WIC 14005.69(h)(4): the individual or their dependent must travel outside their community for an extended period to receive medical services necessary to treat a serious or complex medical condition that is not available in their community of residence, and the individual requests the exemption.
